releaseNote.summary: Adds attributes.rowSecurity: optional, deny-by-default row rules for the instance list, GET and GetInstance(s) tasks. Breaking: a flow lookup error now fails those reads.

rowSecurity.description: A flow declares attributes.rowSecurity.rules (role-keyed row filters in the list-engine filter language, with $.context.Headers / QueryParameters / CurrentUser parameters and the $InstanceStarter / $InstanceBehalfOfStarter identity rules). There is no default: a flow with rowSecurity is deny by default, and 'role X sees everything' is an explicit unfiltered rule; a flow without it is not filtered. A caller sees the OR of the matched static rules' filters plus declared identity rules, ANDed with their own filter; a failed role resolution yields no rows at all, and a failed parameter drops only the rule that reads it; neither ever widens the result. The rule set is the flow's default version (sys-version-registry pointer) when set, else the latest, read with GetFlowAsync(domain, workflow, null) for instances of every version. The public instance list (including groupBy and aggregations), the single GET endpoint (an excluded instance answers the same 404 as a missing one, before the ETag) and the GetInstances / GetInstance tasks (same- and cross-domain, with the task's credential) apply it. The GetInstanceData task, view content resolution, transitions and direct triggers read unfiltered. Behaviour change for EVERY flow, opted in or not (D5, requester-confirmed 2026-10-27): the list, GET and those tasks now perform one cached flow lookup, and a lookup failure other than 'no definition' (for example Instance:100052 409 invalid default-version pointer, Instance:100053 503 version registry unavailable, Instance:100051 flow version not activated) fails the read with that error as is, tagged vnext.rowsecurity.outcome=denied-flow-load with warning 20509; before, the list served rows and GET did not look the flow up. Without its flow no instance of it is readable; starts and transitions of that flow already fail with the same error. When the lookup succeeds, a flow without rowSecurity answers exactly as before. The component cache keys gain a shape segment, so the first reads after the upgrade miss the cache once. Requires a gateway that strips or overwrites the role header and every header a rule reads; QueryParameters are client-controlled. Publish warnings (RS-W*) are log-only. A runtime older than this release ignores rowSecurity entirely and serves every row; the only protections on rollback are not rolling back below this release, or blocking/authorizing the list and GET of those flows at the gateway. Requires the runtime version that ships this entry and a vnext-schema release containing workflow.attributes.rowSecurity.

migrations.title: Instance list, GET and GetInstance(s) tasks fail when the flow definition cannot be loaded
migrations.description: Applies to every flow, with or without rowSecurity. These reads now look the flow up once (cached, GetFlowAsync with no version: the sys-version-registry default version, else the latest). A lookup failure other than 'no definition' fails the read with that error as is: Instance:100052 (409, invalid default-version pointer), Instance:100053 (503, version registry unavailable) or Instance:100051 (flow version not activated). The read is tagged vnext.rowsecurity.outcome=denied-flow-load and logs warning 20509. Before, the list served rows and GET did not look the flow up. A flow with no published definition, and a successful lookup of a flow without rowSecurity, answer exactly as before.
migrations.action: Before upgrading, check that every flow's sys-version-registry default-version pointer resolves to a published version (or is 'latest') and that the version registry is reachable; starts and transitions of such a flow already fail with the same error. Watch warning 20509 after the rollout.

knownIssues.title: rowSecurity filters the instance list, single GET and GetInstances/GetInstance tasks only; functions, transitions and GetInstanceData serve excluded instances by id, and GET 404 next to data 200 is an existence oracle.
knownIssues.workaround: Do not treat rowSecurity as an access boundary for an instance whose id the caller knows; enforce access to those functions at the gateway (authorize) until instance-addressed coverage ships.
knownIssues.description: rowSecurity filters the list and single GET endpoints and the GetInstances/GetInstance tasks only; state/data/view/schema/master/history/internal functions, transitions, view resolution and the GetInstanceData task read excluded instances unfiltered.
